title: AI Infrastructure to Drive India's IT Spending to Rs 16.9 Trillion in 2027
excerpt: Gartner forecasts 10.6% growth in India's IT spending next year, with cloud infrastructure up 40.3% and data centre systems up 28.4% as hyperscalers and global capability centres expand AI capacity.
body:
• India's IT spending is forecast to reach Rs 16.9 trillion in 2027, up 10.6% from 2026, according to Gartner's latest forecast released on November 17, 2026.
  • Cloud infrastructure is the fastest-growing segment: infrastructure as a service (IaaS) spending is forecast to rise 40.3%, and data centre systems spending 28.4%, as hyperscalers build AI compute capacity in India.
  • Software spending is forecast to reach Rs 2.6 trillion, up 19.3%, driven by AI-enabled applications and cloud platforms; IT services will reach a similar Rs 2.6 trillion but grow only 6.2%.
  • For India's tech workforce, Gartner says demand is shifting from traditional services engagements toward higher-value AI consulting, implementation and advisory work.

India's spending on information technology will reach Rs 16.9 trillion in 2027, an increase of 10.6% from 2026, according to the latest forecast by Gartner, released during the firm's IT Symposium/Xpo on November 17. The forecast puts total spending at Rs 16,940,974 million in 2027, against Rs 15,320,328 million in 2026.

The growth is concentrated in the infrastructure that artificial intelligence runs on. Gartner forecasts spending on infrastructure as a service (IaaS) will see the largest growth of any segment in 2027, increasing 40.3% to Rs 815,750 million, followed by data centre systems, forecast to grow 28.4% to Rs 1,206,292 million (about Rs 1.21 trillion).

"India is entering a new phase of technology investment where AI infrastructure and digital sovereignty are becoming strategic priorities. AI is no longer being treated as a standalone technology investment and is becoming a foundational layer for business growth and digital competitiveness."

— DD Mishra, VP Analyst, Gartner

Where the money goes

Mishra attributed the growth to the expansion of global capability centres (GCCs), growing demand for AI-optimised infrastructure and cloud services, and investments in cybersecurity, sovereign capabilities and data modernisation. Software spending is forecast to reach Rs 2.6 trillion in 2027, increasing 19.3% from 2026, driven by demand for AI-enabled applications, cloud software platforms and business applications.

The two largest segments by value grow the slowest. Devices spending is forecast at Rs 6,256,915 million, up 6.3%, and communications services at Rs 3,453,435 million, up 5.3%. IT services spending will reach Rs 2.6 trillion in 2027, Gartner forecasts, as organisations require services to implement AI technologies and navigate complex technology changes — but its 6.2% growth lags the infrastructure and software segments, The Hindu BusinessLine noted in its report on the forecast.

Hyperscalers and government demand

"IaaS continues to experience strong demand across user segments, particularly in sectors such as financial services and government, which require continued expansion of cloud infrastructure to support growing digital needs," said Naresh Singh, Senior Director Analyst at Gartner. He said data centre providers and global hyperscalers have committed significant investments in data centre infrastructure, supported by government policies and incentives for cloud and AI, expanding India's compute capacity and advancing its ambition to become a global hub for AI infrastructure and applications.

BusinessLine reported that government and financial services are emerging as two major drivers of infrastructure spending alongside hyperscalers, with government support, long-term tax incentives and state-level investment incentives contributing to the expansion.

What it means for India's IT services model

The shift carries a warning for India's traditional technology advantage. Mishra told BusinessLine that AI is changing the equation behind the labour-arbitrage model — a large, relatively cost-effective workforce — with "intelligence arbitrage" emerging as a new competitive factor. In Gartner's own release, Mishra said demand is shifting toward higher-value consulting, implementation and advisory services as AI adoption matures, while software platforms with embedded AI capabilities, particularly in the midmarket segment, reshape demand for traditional services engagements.

Gartner said its IT spending forecast is based on analysis of sales by more than a thousand vendors across IT products and services, using primary research complemented by secondary research sources. The figures are forecasts, not reported results, and Gartner revises them quarterly; the underlying research is published in its Market Databook, 3Q26 Update.
